text: This new model is INSANE. Literally AGI. Every job is over by Friday. If you're not building on it you're already dead. 🚀🚀🚀

Ran the new model on our internal eval (1,200 support tickets, 3 labels). It went 71.2% -> 73.9% over the previous release, but calibration got worse: ECE 0.04 -> 0.09, so the 'automate above 0.9' rule now lets through 2x the errors. Impressive on paper, not a drop-in for us yet.
Just tried the new agent framework. Game changer. 100x productivity. Mind-blowing. Nothing else comes close. Trust me.

The agent framework demo is cute, but the eval only counts tasks the agent finished, not tasks it gave up on (about 40% in their own appendix table 3). Success-of-completed is not success. Would love to see pass@1 over all attempted tasks and the cost per task.
Everyone who doubted LLMs is about to look SO stupid. This changes everything. Revolutionary. We are so back.

I disagree with the 'scaling is all you need' take. Three reasons: (1) the loss curves in the paper flatten after 10^24 FLOPs on the reasoning subset, (2) the gains on held-out benchmarks are within the run-to-run noise they report in appendix B, (3) inference cost scales with the same exponent. Not saying scaling is dead, saying the evidence here doesn't support the headline.
Every single person who voted for this bill is a brain-dead clown who hates their own country. Pathetic. Disgrace. They should all be ashamed to show their faces.

I think the bill is a mistake, and here's why: section 4 removes the appeals window entirely rather than shortening it, the CBO estimate assumes 2019 enrollment numbers, and the pilot it cites was in a state with a different funding structure. Happy to be corrected on any of these.
The other side are literally evil morons who want you dead. Anyone who defends them is a traitor. Wake up, idiots.

The zoning reform critics have a point I hadn't considered: the comparable city they cite added 12k units but rents only fell after a separate transit line opened two years later. So the causal story is muddier than the op-ed claims. Still think the reform is net positive, but the evidence is weaker than I thought.
Imagine being so stupid you believe THIS. These people are a disgrace and destroying the country on purpose. Absolute clowns, all of them.

The minister's speech gets the numbers wrong: unemployment fell from 6.1% to 5.4%, not 'halved', and the period she picked starts at the pandemic peak. The underlying trend is real but the framing overstates it by a lot.
Our new phone is the most revolutionary device ever created. Insane camera. Unbelievable battery. You have NEVER seen anything like this. Preorder now!!!

Benchmarked the new phone against last year's: Geekbench 6 multi-core 7,102 vs 6,540 (+8.6%), battery rundown test 14h12m vs 13h40m, camera low-light noise measurably lower at ISO 3200 in our controlled shots. Solid but incremental upgrade. Methodology in the linked post.
This database is 1000x faster than anything on the market. Blows Postgres out of the water. Everyone is switching. Don't get left behind.

Tested the new database's '1000x faster' claim with TPC-C at scale factor 100 on identical c6i.4xlarge boxes: 41k tpmC vs Postgres 16 at 38k. Faster, yes, by ~8%, and only with fsync off. With durability on it was slower. Reproduction scripts in the repo.
Just launched. The best productivity app ever built. Period. Life-changing. You will never go back. Link below.

Used the new productivity app for two weeks. Sync conflicts on 3 of ~200 edits (all when offline on two devices), export loses nested checklists, and the search index took 40s to rebuild on a 5k-note library. The core editor is genuinely fast though. Not switching yet because of the export issue.

Made sourdough for the first time this weekend. Crumb was a bit tight, probably underproofed. Going to try a longer bulk ferment next time.

New paper out: we measure how often code LLMs reproduce license-restricted snippets verbatim. Short version: 0.8% of generations over 50 tokens, concentrated in a handful of popular libraries. Paper and dataset linked.
Reminder that the library closes at 6pm on Sundays now, not 8pm. The change started this month.
